correctness.rationale: For alpha>-1 set q=alpha+1 and x_n=(n+1)/(n+q+1). Orthogonal monomial projection yields explicit one-step coefficients u_n=sqrt(x_n), v_n=x_n sqrt(x_{n-1}). The self-commutator has exactly diagonal |a|^2 A_n+|b|^2 B_n and distance-two bands a conjugate(b) C_n, with A_n=x_n-x_{n-1}, B_n=x_n^2 x_{n-1}-x_n x_{n+1}^2, C_n=sqrt(x_n x_{n+1})(x_{n+2}-x_{n+1}). The exact positive-coefficient rational identity proves B_n>-3A_n; C_n+C_{n-2}<2A_n proves positivity for |a|>=3|b| by band diagonal dominance, including equality. Since n^2(A_n,B_n,C_n)/q tends to (1,-3,1), long alternating-phase test vectors have negative quadratic form whenever |a|/|b|<3. These arguments cover all complex phases, all n and the full Hilbert space; supplementary CHECK.py passed 22332 finite assertions, not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2017, 2021, 2022 and 2023 primary sources do not state this sharp universal necessary-and-sufficient threshold. Kim–Lee 2022 is the closest exact-space two-term class: the opposite-angular Theorem 2.8 yields only a scalar necessary estimate, whereas its positive sufficiency hypotheses exclude the present degree configuration. The present full off-diagonal coupling yields the strictly stronger factor 3. value.rationale: The lowest-degree bounded nonharmonic two-term symbol with genuinely opposite angular shift directions is a natural minimal test case in the program of characterizing Bergman Toeplitz hyponormality. Existing necessary diagonal tests miss an entire forbidden interval sqrt(3)<=|a|/|b|<3; the new full all-vector classification resolves that concrete gap, gives a sharp weight-independent constant for an infinite family of Bergman spaces, and explicitly identifies cross-band interactions as the mechanism. Not merely a renamed harmonic-pair criterion, small numerical gain, or arbitrary finite computation.
